Q: Is there an equivalent to SELECT t1.* when there is a USING() clause? A:

Yes, you have to name every column if your query has a join with USING().

When a query has USING(), the columns of the same name in both tables is reduced to one column in the query result. It no longer belongs to either table.

This means you can't use column qualifiers like tl.TASK_ID.

The same rule applies if you try to use SELECT tl.*. It tries to expand to a list of columns including tl.TASK_ID, but that's not a valid column.

You can use SELECT * because that expands to all columns, and it doesn't matter that it includes the de-duplicated column used for the join condition.

Anyway, it's generally a good practice to avoid wildcards in SQL queries.

Q: How to get CSS to select ID that begins with a string (not in Javascript)? A: 
[id^=product]

^= indicates "starts with". Conversely, $= indicates "ends with".

The symbols are actually borrowed from Regex syntax, where ^ and $ mean "start of string" and "end of string" respectively.

See the specs for full information: Substring matching attribute selectors - W3C

By the way, you can also do "does not start with" like this: :not([id^=product])

Q: Can I pass Paginated Report Matrix Values to a Power App form? A:

You can’t “pass matrix values” directly from a paginated report, but you can pass them via the URL.

In Power BI Report Builder, create an Action → Go to URL on the matrix (or textbox) and construct a URL to your Power App like this:

https://apps.powerapps.com/play/appId=XXX&IDs=1,2,3

You would need to construct that comma-separated ID list in your report (using an expression on the filtered data set).

Then in Power Apps, retrieve the parameter value like this:

Param("IDs")

And filter your SharePoint list like this:

Filter(
  MyList,
  ID in Split(Param("IDs"), ",").Result
)

This way, the app will only load the IDs that were displayed in the paginated report after the user applied the parameters.

One thing to keep in mind is that if your ID list is large enough, you could run into URL length limits. In that case, it’s probably easier to pass the same filter parameter(s) and reapply the filter logic in your app.
